facts: Shinjuku Station is the busiest train station in the world, handling millions of passengers daily.
Shinjuku Gyoen is a peaceful national garden that offers stunning cherry blossoms in spring and lush greenery year-round.
The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku offers free panoramic views of the city and Mount Fuji.
Kabukicho is Shinjuku's famous entertainment district, vibrant with neon lights, restaurants, and theaters.
Omoide Yokocho, or Memory Lane, retains a charming retro post-war vibe with tiny yakitori stalls and alleyways.
Golden Gai features over two hundred tiny bars squeezed into six narrow micro-alleys, preserving old Tokyo charm.
The perimeter around Shinjuku Gyoen offers a popular, scenic loop for local runners seeking a green escape.
Godzilla's massive head peaks over the Toho Cinema building, making it a famous pop-culture landmark in Kabukicho.
Shinjuku began as a post station along the Koshu Kaido highway during Japan's Edo period.
Shinjuku is a major shopping hub housing giant department stores like Isetan and Takashimaya Times Square.
The Sompo Museum of Art in Shinjuku famously houses one of Vincent van Gogh's Sunflowers paintings.
Central Park in Shinjuku provides a cool green oasis right behind the soaring metropolitan skyscraper complex.
Shinjuku is famous for its vibrant ramen culture, featuring dozens of renowned noodle shops representing diverse styles.
The Tokyo Marathon route passes through the bustling streets of Shinjuku near its starting area.
The Mode Gakuen Cocoon Tower is an iconic, award-winning 50-story skyscraper designed like a giant cocoon.
Hanazono Shrine is a historic Shinto shrine hidden amidst Shinjuku's skyscrapers, hosting colorful seasonal festivals.
Depachika, the underground food halls in Shinjuku's department stores, offer incredible gourmet treats from across Japan.
After a major earthquake in 1923, Shinjuku rapidly grew because its sturdy ground safely resisted heavy seismic damage.
Shinjuku Ni-chome is widely known as Tokyo's primary center for LGBTQ+ culture and nightlife.
During autumn, the Japanese maple trees in Shinjuku Gyoen turn brilliant shades of crimson and gold.
